---
title: "Chart series"
---

The DSA figures are row series on `Chart Data` columns `D:X`, with projection
years in the row-35 headers. The package publishes those rows as tensors keyed
by `SCENARIO` and `TIME_PERIOD`.

Two families matter for a write-up:

- **Figure series** used by `Output 2-1` / `Output 2-2` (baseline, historical
  average, the most-extreme standardized-and-tailored shock, the one-year
  shock used only in the chart, and the threshold).
- **Public-debt stress blocks** -- PV of debt-to-GDP, PV of debt-to-revenue,
  debt service-to-revenue, and debt service-to-GDP -- each with the full
  scenario ladder (Baseline, A1 historical, B1-B6, C1-C4, A2 customized).

External figures additionally cover PV of debt-to-exports and debt service to
exports. The public-debt ladder and the external figure for the same ratio are
different Chart Data rows; do not mix them in one plot.

# A figure path

Figure R61 is the PV of public debt to GDP shown with the short figure
scenario list. The template snapshot is enough to evaluate it.

```{python}
import inspect

import polars as pl

from lic_dsf_2025_08_12 import as_records, data
from lic_dsf_2025_08_12.api import (
    compute_chart_output_chart_data_figure_r61_pv_debt_gdp_ratio,
)


def template_inputs(compute):
    return {
        name: getattr(data, f"{name.upper()}_DEFAULT")
        for name in inspect.signature(compute).parameters
    }


compute = compute_chart_output_chart_data_figure_r61_pv_debt_gdp_ratio
path = compute(**template_inputs(compute))
print(path.domain.axes[0].name, path.domain.axes[0].keys)
print(
    path.domain.axes[1].name,
    path.domain.axes[1].keys[:6],
    "...",
    len(path.domain.axes[1].keys),
    "years",
)
```

`as_records` zips those coordinates onto the values. That is safer than
walking a tuple by index, because a later vintage can add a year without
changing the meaning of `TIME_PERIOD == 2028`.

```{python}
records = as_records(compute, path, measure="pv_debt_gdp")
frame = pl.DataFrame(records)
frame.filter(pl.col("TIME_PERIOD") <= 2028)
```

# Select one scenario

`sel` drops the fixed axis and leaves a year path you can index by calendar
year:

```{python}
baseline = path.sel(SCENARIO="Baseline")
threshold = path.sel(SCENARIO="Threshold")
print(baseline[2024], threshold[2024])
print(baseline[2030], threshold[2030])
```

```{python}
from matplotlib import pyplot as plt

years = list(baseline.domain.axes[0].keys)
fig, ax = plt.subplots()
for scenario in path.domain.axes[0].keys:
    series = path.sel(SCENARIO=scenario)
    ax.plot(years, [series[year] for year in years], label=scenario)
ax.set_xlabel("Year")
ax.set_ylabel("PV of debt to GDP")
ax.set_title("Chart Data figure R61, template snapshot")
ax.legend(fontsize=8)
plt.show()
```

# The public-debt ladder

The long stress block for the same concept is a different function and a
different Chart Data row. Its scenario axis is the full B/C ladder:

```{python}
from lic_dsf_2025_08_12.api import (
    compute_chart_output_chart_data_pv_of_debt_to_gdp_ratio_pv_debt_to_gdp,
)

ladder_fn = compute_chart_output_chart_data_pv_of_debt_to_gdp_ratio_pv_debt_to_gdp
ladder = ladder_fn(**template_inputs(ladder_fn))
print(ladder.domain.axes[0].keys)
print("baseline 2024 on the ladder:", ladder.sel(SCENARIO="Baseline")[2024])
print("baseline 2024 on figure R61:", baseline[2024])
```

The two 2024 baseline numbers differ because they are different published rows
(the public-debt stress block versus the figure series). Say which row you are
plotting.

# Customized A2 paths

Each stress block has a companion
`compute_chart_*_a2_alternative_scenario_customize_enter` function for the A2
customized rung. Those functions take the `customized_public_*` and
`customized_external_*` leaves in addition to the standard Input 3-8 surface.
Leave the template customized deltas at zero unless you are actually running
an alternative scenario.

# Published chart functions

| Function | Typical use |
| --- | --- |
| `compute_chart_output_chart_data_figure_r61_pv_debt_gdp_ratio` | Figure PV debt/GDP |
| `compute_chart_output_chart_data_figure_r103_pv_debt_to_exports` | Figure PV debt/exports |
| `compute_chart_output_chart_data_figure_r145_debt_service_to_exports` | Figure debt service/exports |
| `compute_chart_output_chart_data_figure_r187_debt_service_to_revenue` | Figure debt service/revenue |
| `compute_chart_output_chart_data_figure_r263_pv_debt_to_gdp` | Additional PV debt/GDP figure row |
| `compute_chart_output_chart_data_figure_r341_debt_service_to_revenue` | Additional debt service/revenue figure row |
| `compute_chart_output_chart_data_pv_of_debt_to_gdp_ratio_pv_debt_to_gdp` | Public-debt PV/GDP ladder |
| `compute_chart_output_chart_data_pv_of_debt_to_revenue_ratio_pv_debt_to_revenue` | Public-debt PV/revenue ladder |
| `compute_chart_output_chart_data_debt_service_to_revenue_ratio_debt_service_to_revenue` | Public-debt service/revenue ladder |
| `compute_chart_output_chart_data_debt_service_to_gdp_ratio_debt_service_gdp_ratio` | Public-debt service/GDP ladder |
| `compute_chart_pv_debt_to_revenue_mx_shock_standard_tailored` | Most-extreme PV/revenue shock path |
| `compute_chart_*_a2_alternative_scenario_customize_enter` | Customized A2 rung for the matching indicator |
